name: MonarchButtonStyle
title: MenuButton
wrapsNative: Menu(content:label:) with .buttonStyle(.monarch(_:size:)) on the Menu; the label is a Text and a chevron.down MonarchIcon
summary: A button that opens a menu of actions: the standard Menu whose trigger takes the Monarch button style.
whenToUse: When a row, card or screen has more related actions than fit as buttons ("Actions", "…"), or an export or sort choice is made from a short list.
whenNotToUse: When one action is the obvious default and the rest are alternatives, use a Menu with primaryAction (split-button). For a value that stays shown, use a Picker. For a long or searchable list, use a sheet with searchable.
api: func buttonStyle(_ style: MonarchButtonStyle) -> some View  // .monarch(_ variant: MonarchButtonVariant = .secondary, size: MonarchButtonSize = .md, fullWidth: Bool = false)

options.name: variant
options.description: On .buttonStyle(.monarch(_:size:fullWidth:)): primary, secondary, ghost or danger. Use ghost for an icon-only trigger.

options.name: size
options.description: sm, md or lg. The touch target is at least 44 points at every size.

options.name: fullWidth
options.description: Whether the trigger fills the available width.

states.name: closed
states.description: The trigger looks like any Monarch button of its variant, with a chevron after the title.

states.name: pressed
states.description: The trigger takes the pressed colour of its variant; the system opens the menu.

states.name: open
states.description: The system menu is shown over the screen; the trigger is not redrawn.

states.name: disabled
states.description: disabled(true) on the Menu uses the disabled colours and the menu does not open.

appearance: The trigger is a Monarch button: the accent fill for primary, the surface with the default border for secondary, no fill for ghost, the danger fill for danger; disabled uses the muted fill and disabled text roles. The menu itself is the system's, in every theme.
platformNotes: The web MenuButton is a Radix DropdownMenu trigger with an items shorthand, controlled open state, alignment, side and a chevron that turns while open. On iOS the system Menu places and animates the menu, takes Button, Toggle, Picker, Divider and nested Menu items, and has no open binding, alignment or side; the chevron does not turn. Links in the menu are Link items. Keyboard shortcut hints are keyboardShortcut(_:) on the items. Android composes the same with its own menu.
accessibility: VoiceOver reads the trigger as a button with the menu's title, and a hint that it opens a menu (system behaviour).
An icon-only trigger needs accessibilityLabel; the recipe and the catalogue give one.
The chevron is decorative (MonarchIcon(systemName:) hides it).
Destructive items use Button(role: .destructive), which the system reads and colours; pair them with a confirmation.
The trigger keeps a 44-point touch target at every size.
edgeCases: A long title wraps inside the trigger rather than widening it past the screen.
On macOS (host builds only) Menu draws a pull-down button and the button style may not apply; iOS is the supported platform.
The menu does not open while the trigger is disabled; there is no loading state, so disable it or show progress elsewhere.
Whether VoiceOver reads the menu hint on every iOS version was not checked on a device.

Icon only, with a spoken name

parityExceptions.reason: The key equivalent comes from .keyboardShortcut("d", modifiers: .command), which the system draws as the command key; the destructive tone is the button role.
parityExceptions.convention: Apple HIG menus: key equivalents are drawn by the system from keyboardShortcut, destructive items use role .destructive
